standard.title: Statistical Investigations with Samples
standard.description: plan and conduct statistical investigations involving samples of a population; use ethical and fair methods to make inferences about the population and report findings, acknowledging uncertainty
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plan and conduct statistical investigations (from AC9M7ST03). Students understand sampling methods and variation (from AC9M8ST02, AC9M8ST03).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan and conduct investigations using ethical and fair sampling methods, make inferences about the population, and report findings while explicitly acknowledging uncertainty.

nodes.label: Planning an ethical investigation with sampling
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students plan a statistical investigation including ethical and fair sampling methods, anticipate sources of uncertainty, and identify how findings will be used to make inferences.
nodes.minimum_width: Plan a statistical investigation specifying: the population, the sampling method, why it is ethical and fair, and what inference is being sought.
nodes.typical_width: Design an investigation with explicit ethical consideration; identify potential sources of bias and uncertainty; plan how to communicate uncertainty in the report.
wider: Investigate progress in reconciliation between First Nations Australians and non-Indigenous Australians — evaluate the ethical considerations in sampling and reporting for such sensitive topics.
Explore how businesses use electricity consumption data to draw conclusions about event impacts (e.g. pandemic effects) — evaluate the ethical data use.

response_modes.reason: Planning an ethical investigation requires explicit reasoning about who is included, who might be harmed by the data collection, and how to minimise bias — students need a planning scaffold that surfaces these considerations.

nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires conducting the investigation and reporting with acknowledged uncertainty — without a valid, ethically-designed plan from Node 1, there is no investigation to conduct and no basis for making or communicating inferences.
success_criteria: Specifies the population, sample, and sampling method.
Identifies at least one ethical consideration and addresses it in the plan.
States what inference will be drawn from the investigation.

nodes.label: Conducting, inferring and reporting with uncertainty
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students conduct the investigation, make inferences about the population from the sample, and report findings while explicitly acknowledging the uncertainty introduced by sampling.
nodes.minimum_width: Conduct a sample investigation; make one inference about the population; state one source of uncertainty in the conclusion.
nodes.typical_width: Conduct a full investigation cycle; make multiple inferences; report findings including confidence language; connect sample size to the degree of uncertainty acknowledged.
wider: Compare the inferences drawn from two different sample sizes for the same population — discuss how the larger sample changes confidence in the inference.
Explore how statistical uncertainty is communicated in public health or environmental reporting — compare with how uncertainty is often omitted in media reports.

response_modes.reason: Conducting and reporting with acknowledged uncertainty integrates sampling method choice, distribution analysis, inference-making, and communication — the full statistics strand at Year 8.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Comparing sample sizes and their effect on inference confidence, or investigating how public reports handle uncertainty, are rich critical statistical thinking tasks for advancing students within Year 8.
success_criteria: Makes a valid inference about the population from the sample.
Explicitly acknowledges uncertainty in the report.
Connects the degree of uncertainty to the sample size and method.
